stem.text: Let \( f(x) = x^{2} - 3 x + 2 \). The functions \( g \) and \( h \) are continuous for all real numbers, with \( g(0) = 1 \), \( g(1) = 2 \), \( g(2) = 0 \), \( g(3) = 0 \), \( g(4) = 2 \), \( h(0) = 1 \), \( h(1) = 1 \), \( h(2) = 3 \), \( h(3) = 1 \), \( h(4) = 4 \). Find the value of \( \lim_{x \to 3} \left[ 2f(g(x)) - 2g(h(x)) - h(f(x)) \right] \).

worked_solution.text: Record the limits. \( f \) is a polynomial and \( g \) and \( h \) are continuous, so \( \lim_{x \to 3} f(x) = f(3) = 2 \), \( \lim_{x \to 3} g(x) = 0 \), and \( \lim_{x \to 3} h(x) = 1 \).

The expression is a sum of constant multiples of three composites. In each composite the outer function is continuous at the limit of the inner one, so \( \lim_{x \to 3} f(g(x)) = f(0) = 2 \), \( \lim_{x \to 3} g(h(x)) = g(1) = 2 \), \( \lim_{x \to 3} h(f(x)) = h(2) = 3 \).
Apply the sum and constant multiple theorems: \( (2)(2) + (-2)(2) + (-1)(3) = -3 \).
